I will keep my land in the usual winter wheat and summer maize rotation. In Quzhou, this is the crop pattern I trust most because I know how to manage it, the machines and inputs are easy to find, and the weather and irrigation conditions fit it better than riskier cash crops. At 62, I want work that is steady and not too complicated, so I will not split into many small crops. I will stay with improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed, put most of my money into fertilizer at the right time, irrigate when the crop is under real need, and keep pesticide use limited to the main disease and insect windows. For tillage, I will use rotary tillage before wheat because it is fast and practical for me, and I will use no-tillage for summer maize after wheat harvest to save time and soil moisture. I am aiming for stable yield more than chasing the highest yield.
